title: Proteomic mapping of ER-PM junctions in living HEK293 cells
protocol: Coat culture dishes with poly-L-lysine.
Rock gently to ensure even coating of the culture surface.
Remove poly-lysine by aspiration after 5 minutes.
Rinse surface with sterile tissue culture grade water five times and remove water.
Dry the plate at 60°C for one hour.
Seed HEK293 cells (2×10^5 cells) in pre-coated 35-mm glass bottom dish and culture for one day.
Transfect GFP-STIM1-APEX2 using Lipofectamine 3000 (500 ng plasmid) following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Remove normal DMEM medium by aspiration and wash with Ca^2+-free HBSS twice; keep cells in HBSS 24 hours post-transfection.
Add TG to a final concentration of 1 μM for 5 minutes to trigger store depletion.
Add biotin-phenol (at a final concentration of 0.5 mM) to the medium for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Add freshly-prepared H2O2 (1 mM) to the medium for exactly one minute at room temperature to initiate biotinylation.
Stop the reaction immediately by washing cells with 2 ml quencher solution for 1 min.
Repeat washing cells with 2 ml quencher solution five times.
Wash cells with 2 ml PBS three times.
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde at room temperature for 30 min.
Rinse with PBS three times.
Treat cells with cold methanol at -20 °C for 10 min.
Rinse with PBS three times.
Block with 5% (w/v) BSA in PBS for 1 h at room temperature, rotating the culture dish gently.
Add streptavidin-Dylight594 (1:2000 dilution) to the blocking buffer and shake gently for 2 h at room temperature; avoid exposure to light.
Wash with PBS ten times to remove unbound streptavidin-DyLight594.
Capture images using a confocal microscope or total internal reflection fluorescence microscope.
Add biotin-phenol at a final concentration of 0.5 mM to the culture medium for 30 minutes at 37 °C.
Replace DMEM medium with Ca²⁺-free HBSS solution after transfection.
Treat cells in 1 μM TG for 5 minutes to trigger store depletion.
Scrap cells from the culture dish and centrifuge at 5,000 × g for 15 minutes.
Lysate cells with RIPA buffer supplemented with 1× protease inhibitor cocktail, then centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes to remove insoluble debris.
Pack NeutrAvidin Agarose Resin into a 1.5 ml tube and wash with RIPA buffer.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 1 minute to remove storage solution.
Repeat the washing step twice.
Equilibrate resin with RIPA buffer for 30 minutes, shaking gently.
Incubate cell lysates with resin at an 8 mg of biotinylated protein/ml of settled resin ratio and gently rotate the mixture for 4-6 hours to enrich biotinylated proteins.
Rinse beads with 1 ml PBS supplemented with 1× protease inhibitor cocktail.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g to remove buffer.
Repeat wash step for ten times to remove unbound proteins.
Discard wash buffer.
Boil resin with LDS sample buffer.
Separate proteins by 4-12% Bis-Tris protein gels.
Elute enriched proteins from beads using elution buffer (8 M urea, pH 1.5).
Centrifuge at 2,000 ×g for 1 min and collect the supernatant to a new clean 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Repeat steps 14-15 and collect the elution proteins into one tube.
Add 6× volume of acetone that is pre-cooled at -20°C.
Mix well and keep at -20°C for 30 min to overnight.
Spin in a refrigerated microfuge at top speed for 30 min.
Aspirate most of the supernatant and leave the last drop to avoid disturbing the pellet.
Wash the pellet with 500 μl cold acetone at -20°C twice.
Air-dry the pellet without using a speed vacuum; over-dried samples are difficult to dissolve.
Cut gel slices to approximately 1 mm³ pieces.
Destain gel slices with 0.1 ml ProteoSilver Destainer A and 0.1 ml ProteoSilver Destainer B.
Wash gel slices with 500 μl of 50 mM NH₄HCO₃ for 20 min; discard the washing buffer.
Add 150 μl of 50 mM NH₄HCO₃ and 0.5 μl of 1 M TCEP to gel slices; incubate at 60°C for 15 min.
Cool to room temperature (RT) and add 2 μl of 500 mM IAA to gel slices; incubate in the dark at RT for 15 min; discard the solvent.
Add 1 ml of acetonitrile to shrink gel pieces; remove the solvent after 10-15 min; dry the gel slices in a speed vacuum.

Reswell gel pieces with 20 μl of Promega modified trypsin (sequencing grade) at a concentration of 5 ng/μl in 25 mM NH₄HCO₃; add 10-20 μl additional buffer to cover the gel slices; incubate overnight at 37°C.
Remove the supernatant and place in new tubes.
Extract remaining peptides from gel with 50 μl extract buffer I (50% Acetonitrile/5% Formic acid) for 30 min in a thermomixer at 700 rpm.
Extract remaining peptides from gel with 50 μl extract buffer II (75% Acetonitrile/0.1% FA) for 30 minutes in a thermomixer at 700 rpm.
Combine the supernatant and two extracts and speed vac to dryness.
Resuspend peptides with 20 μl 0.1% formic acid.
Dissolve proteins in 8 M urea, 100 mM Tris pH 8.5 (10 ul).
Sonicate for 10 min.
Add TCEP to a final concentration of 5 mM and incubate at RT for 20 min.
Add IAA to a final concentration of 10 mM; incubate at RT for 15 min in the dark.
Dilute samples by a factor of 4 with 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.5.
Add CaCl₂ to a final concentration of 1 mM.
Add methylamine to 20 mM to reduce carbamylation.
Add trypsin with an enzyme:substrate ratio of 1:50.
Incubate at 37 ºC O/N in the dark.
Add formic acid to 4~5% (final concentration).
Centrifuge at 18,000 xg for 30 min, and save the supernatant for LC-MS/MS.
Load peptides on a pre-column \(75 mm ID, 8 cm long) packed with ODS-AQ 120 Å, 10 mm reversed-phase beads.
Separate peptides on an analytical column \(75 mm ID, 11 cm long) packed with Luna C18 100 Å, 1.8 mm resin.
Perform acetonitrile gradient from 0–28% in 55 min and 28-80% in another 6 min \(with 0.1% FA in the mobile phase).
Operate HPLC at a flow rate of 200 nl/min.
Isolate top 15 most intense precursor ions for HCD MS2 with resolution 17,500 and normalized collision energy 27.
Exclude dynamic exclusion time of 20 s for precursor ions of a 1+, > 6+ or unassigned charge state.
Search MS2 spectra against the Uniprot-human database using ProLuCID with mass accuracy set to 50 ppm for both precursor and fragment ions.
Apply carbamidomethylation on cysteine as a fixed modification.
Filter ProLuCID search results using DTASelect 2.0 with a 1% FDR cutoff at the spectral level.
Require at least two peptides for identifying a protein.
Ensure the protein-level FDR is less than 1%.
Discard hits detected in control groups.
Select positive hits that are detected in at least two out of four repeated experiments.
